PPWR-MINIMISATION.title: PPWR - Packaging minimisation
PPWR-MINIMISATION.summary: PPWR Article 10(1) requires packaging weight and volume to be reduced to the minimum necessary for functionality, taking account of the packaging's shape and material.
PPWR-MINIMISATION.supports: PPWR Article 10(1) requires packaging weight and volume to be reduced to the minimum necessary for functionality, taking account of the packaging's shape and material.

PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.title: PPWR - Minimum recycled content
PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.summary: PPWR Article 7 establishes minimum recycled-content requirements for plastic packaging according to the relevant packaging type and format; the threshold must be selected from the legal category rather than assumed to be uniform for all cosmetic bottles.
PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.supports: PPWR Article 7 establishes minimum recycled-content requirements for plastic packaging according to the relevant packaging type and format; the threshold must be selected from the legal category rather than assumed to be uniform for all cosmetic bottles.
PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.citation: Article 7(1) and Article 7(8); Annex II, Table 1
PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.effectiveDate: 1 January 2030 or 3 years after entry into force of the implementing act referred to in Article 7(8), whichever is later
PPWR-RECYCLED-CONTENT.effective_date: 1 January 2030 or 3 years after entry into force of the implementing act referred to in Article 7(8), whichever is later

PPWR-LABELLING.title: PPWR - Packaging material labelling
PPWR-LABELLING.summary: Article 12(1) provides for a harmonised label identifying packaging material composition to facilitate consumer sorting, subject to the statutory start date and implementing acts.
PPWR-LABELLING.supports: Article 12(1) provides for a harmonised label identifying packaging material composition to facilitate consumer sorting, subject to the statutory start date and implementing acts.
PPWR-LABELLING.effectiveDate: 12 August 2028 or 24 months after entry into force of implementing acts under Article 12(6) or (7), whichever is later
PPWR-LABELLING.effective_date: 12 August 2028 or 24 months after entry into force of implementing acts under Article 12(6) or (7), whichever is later

PPWR-RECYCLABILITY.title: PPWR - Design for recycling
PPWR-RECYCLABILITY.summary: Article 6 establishes the recyclability framework, including design-for-recycling criteria and recycling-at-scale milestones; the criteria and grades are phased in rather than applying as one undifferentiated deadline.
PPWR-RECYCLABILITY.supports: Article 6 establishes the recyclability framework, including design-for-recycling criteria and recycling-at-scale milestones; the criteria and grades are phased in rather than applying as one undifferentiated deadline.
PPWR-RECYCLABILITY.effectiveDate: Generally from 1 January 2030 or 24 months after the relevant delegated acts enter into force, whichever is later; further recycling-at-scale milestone in 2035; grades A or B required from 1 January 2038, subject to the regulation's details and exceptions
PPWR-RECYCLABILITY.effective_date: Generally from 1 January 2030 or 24 months after the relevant delegated acts enter into force, whichever is later; further recycling-at-scale milestone in 2035; grades A or B required from 1 January 2038, subject to the regulation's details and exceptions

EU-ECGT.title: Directive (EU) 2024/825 - Generic environmental claims and offsetting claims
EU-ECGT.summary: The Directive targets generic environmental claims that cannot be substantiated by relevant recognised excellent environmental performance, and separately prohibits product greenhouse-gas neutrality, reduction, or positivity claims based on offsetting.
EU-ECGT.supports: The Directive targets generic environmental claims that cannot be substantiated by relevant recognised excellent environmental performance, and separately prohibits product greenhouse-gas neutrality, reduction, or positivity claims based on offsetting.
EU-ECGT.citation: Article 1(4), amending Annex I to Directive 2005/29/EC, points 2a and 4a-4c; Recital 9 for examples of generic claims
EU-ECGT.effectiveDate: Applies from 27 September 2026; check national implementation for the intended market
EU-ECGT.effective_date: Applies from 27 September 2026; check national implementation for the intended market

EU-COSMETICS.title: Cosmetics Regulation - Safety and packaging labelling
EU-COSMETICS.summary: Article 19 requires specified product and consumer information on cosmetic-product containers and packaging, while Article 3 establishes the general cosmetics safety requirement under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use.
EU-COSMETICS.supports: Article 19 requires specified product and consumer information on cosmetic-product containers and packaging, while Article 3 establishes the general cosmetics safety requirement under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use.
EU-COSMETICS.effectiveDate: General application date 11 July 2013, subject to subsequent amendments and current applicable text
EU-COSMETICS.effective_date: General application date 11 July 2013, subject to subsequent amendments and current applicable text

TECH-CARTON-REMOVAL.title: Outer-carton removal - Transit damage validation
TECH-CARTON-REMOVAL.summary: ISTA Procedure 3A is a general simulation performance test for packaged products shipped individually through parcel-delivery systems; it does not establish a universal rule that a shampoo bottle is safe to ship without an outer carton.
TECH-CARTON-REMOVAL.supports: ISTA Procedure 3A is a general simulation performance test for packaged products shipped individually through parcel-delivery systems; it does not establish a universal rule that a shampoo bottle is safe to ship without an outer carton.
TECH-CARTON-REMOVAL.citation: ISTA Test Procedures page, General Simulation Tests, Procedure 3A: Parcel Delivery System Shipments 150 lb (70 kg) or Less

TECH-SLEEVE-LABEL.title: Full-body shrink sleeve - Bottle sorting and recyclability
TECH-SLEEVE-LABEL.summary: Sleeves can interfere with bottle identification and recyclate quality, but the effect depends on sleeve material, colour, coverage, perforation, and the specific recycling stream; the sources do not establish that every sleeve is unrecyclable.
TECH-SLEEVE-LABEL.supports: Sleeves can interfere with bottle identification and recyclate quality, but the effect depends on sleeve material, colour, coverage, perforation, and the specific recycling stream; the sources do not establish that every sleeve is unrecyclable.
TECH-SLEEVE-LABEL.citation: RECOUP, Recyclability of Bottles with Sleeves, Version 8, p. 2 and relevant discussion of detection, sleeve materials, and solutions. Secondary source: https://recyclass.eu/protocols-guidelines/design-for-recycling-guidelines/packaging/ (RecyClass current Packaging Design for Recycling Guidelines)

TECH-PUMP-METAL.title: Mono-material pump - Plastic spring/ball alternative
TECH-PUMP-METAL.summary: RecyClass reports that a specific fully plastic, polyolefin-based pump with a plastic spring and ball was tested as compatible with the HDPE recycling stream under a stated condition that the pump not exceed 26% of total packaging weight; this does not establish that every metal-spring pump makes a bottle unrecyclable.
TECH-PUMP-METAL.supports: RecyClass reports that a specific fully plastic, polyolefin-based pump with a plastic spring and ball was tested as compatible with the HDPE recycling stream under a stated condition that the pump not exceed 26% of total packaging weight; this does not establish that every metal-spring pump makes a bottle unrecyclable.
TECH-PUMP-METAL.citation: RecyClass, Apackaging Group receives a RecyClass Recyclability Approval for Infinity Pump; stated HDPE-container evaluation protocol and pump weight condition. Secondary source: https://aptar.com/en-us/products/future-fully-recyclable-dispensing-pump (Aptar Beauty, Future - Fully Recyclable Dispensing Pump)

TECH-PCR-AVAILABILITY.title: PCR PET - Commercial availability for cosmetic bottles
TECH-PCR-AVAILABILITY.summary: Supplier catalogues list PET cosmetics/personal-care bottles with PCR options; ALPLA lists a 500 mL cosmetics bottle configurable up to 100% rPET with an MOQ of 35,000 units, demonstrating an actual commercial offering but not universal availability, price, colour, odour, or formulation compatibility.
TECH-PCR-AVAILABILITY.supports: Supplier catalogues list PET cosmetics/personal-care bottles with PCR options; ALPLA lists a 500 mL cosmetics bottle configurable up to 100% rPET with an MOQ of 35,000 units, demonstrating an actual commercial offering but not universal availability, price, colour, odour, or formulation compatibility.
TECH-PCR-AVAILABILITY.citation: ALPLA Standard Products, 500 ml Cosmetics Bottle 27 g, product specification including PCR options and MOQ. Secondary source: https://packagingsolutions.amcor.com/en/product/product-item/250ml-european-pet-13823010 (Amcor Packaging Solutions, 250ml European PET)

TECH-FLEX-POUCH.title: Refill pouches - Flexible packaging recycling route
TECH-FLEX-POUCH.summary: CEFLEX guidance prefers mono-PE or mono-PP flexible structures over mixed-material structures for improved sortability and recycling performance, but this does not prove a universal EU collection and recycling route for every refill pouch.
TECH-FLEX-POUCH.supports: CEFLEX guidance prefers mono-PE or mono-PP flexible structures over mixed-material structures for improved sortability and recycling performance, but this does not prove a universal EU collection and recycling route for every refill pouch.
TECH-FLEX-POUCH.citation: CEFLEX D4ACE Guidelines, Design Principles and Design Choices. Secondary source: https://www.ellenmacarthurfoundation.org/tackling-flexible-plastic-packaging-waste (Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Tackling Flexible Plastic Packaging Waste)

TECH-ALU-LINING.title: Aluminium bottle - Internal lacquer and product compatibility
TECH-ALU-LINING.summary: Supplier guidance describes internal linings for aluminium toiletry bottles and identifies formulation pH, fragrance/oils, alcohol, surfactant system, filling process, closure, and shelf life as compatibility considerations; it does not establish that every shampoo needs the same lacquer or that a coating is universally compatible with recycling.
TECH-ALU-LINING.supports: Supplier guidance describes internal linings for aluminium toiletry bottles and identifies formulation pH, fragrance/oils, alcohol, surfactant system, filling process, closure, and shelf life as compatibility considerations; it does not establish that every shampoo needs the same lacquer or that a coating is universally compatible with recycling.
TECH-ALU-LINING.citation: PPG, PPG launches non-BPA PPG HOBA coatings for aluminum bottles at Paris Packaging Week (3 February 2025). Secondary source: https://blueskysolutionsuk.com/insight-resource/aluminium-packaging-for-toiletries/ (BlueSky Solutions, Aluminium Packaging for Toiletries, sections on internal lacquer/lining and compatibility)

TECH-GLASS-TRANSPORT.title: Glass versus plastic - Transport emissions for 250 mL shampoo
TECH-GLASS-TRANSPORT.summary: No reliable source was verified that quantifies the transport-only emissions difference between otherwise comparable 250 mL glass and plastic shampoo bottles under a defined EU distribution scenario.
TECH-GLASS-TRANSPORT.supports: No reliable source was verified that quantifies the transport-only emissions difference between otherwise comparable 250 mL glass and plastic shampoo bottles under a defined EU distribution scenario.

TECH-PLA-EOL.title: Rigid PLA - EU sorting/recycling and end-of-life route
TECH-PLA-EOL.summary: CBE JU reports industrial sorting trials involving PLA cups/trays and other bio-based plastic items, while the European Commission describes the wider end-of-life policy context; these sources indicate infrastructure and sorting considerations but do not prove that rigid PLA bottles are compostable-only or universally accepted in EU kerbside streams.
TECH-PLA-EOL.supports: CBE JU reports industrial sorting trials involving PLA cups/trays and other bio-based plastic items, while the European Commission describes the wider end-of-life policy context; these sources indicate infrastructure and sorting considerations but do not prove that rigid PLA bottles are compostable-only or universally accepted in EU kerbside streams.
TECH-PLA-EOL.citation: CBE JU, Sorting out the future of bio-based plastics recycling, published 21 August 2026, sections Testing under real-world conditions, Results at industrial scale, and What's next. Secondary source: https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/plastics/bio-based-biodegradable-and-compostable-plastics_en (European Commission, EU policy framework on biobased, biodegradable and compostable plastics)

TECH-RECYCLABILITY-RIGID-PLASTIC.title: Rigid PET, HDPE and PP - Recyclability baseline
TECH-RECYCLABILITY-RIGID-PLASTIC.summary: RecyClass maintains stream-specific design-for-recycling guidance for PET bottles and HDPE/PP containers; an individual package's recyclability depends on its full design, components, applicable stream, and relevant PPWR criteria rather than polymer identity alone.
TECH-RECYCLABILITY-RIGID-PLASTIC.supports: RecyClass maintains stream-specific design-for-recycling guidance for PET bottles and HDPE/PP containers; an individual package's recyclability depends on its full design, components, applicable stream, and relevant PPWR criteria rather than polymer identity alone.
TECH-RECYCLABILITY-RIGID-PLASTIC.citation: RecyClass current Packaging Design for Recycling Guidelines. Secondary source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32025R0040 (PPWR Article 6(1)-(5) and Article 6(8), Recyclable packaging)

PK01.title: Monopolymer Polyethylene Design Guidelines
PK01.summary: Monopolymer PE structures simplify recycling streams and eliminate multi-material laminates.
PK01.supports: Monopolymer PE structures simplify recycling streams and eliminate multi-material laminates.

PK02.title: Recycled Content Integration Standards
PK02.summary: Incorporating post-consumer recycled (PCR) resin reduces carbon footprint while maintaining barrier properties.
PK02.supports: Incorporating post-consumer recycled (PCR) resin reduces carbon footprint while maintaining barrier properties.

PK03.title: Outer Carton Elimination Impact
PK03.summary: Removing secondary paperboard cartons directly decreases packaging mass per unit without material reformulation.
PK03.supports: Removing secondary paperboard cartons directly decreases packaging mass per unit without material reformulation.

PK04.title: Glass vs. Flexible Plastic Carbon Life Cycle
PK04.summary: Flexible pouches and mono-materials demonstrate significantly lower transport emissions than rigid glass.
PK04.supports: Flexible pouches and mono-materials demonstrate significantly lower transport emissions than rigid glass.

PK05.title: Refillable Container Systems Assessment
PK05.summary: Refill models reduce single-use container waste across repeated consumer lifecycles.
PK05.supports: Refill models reduce single-use container waste across repeated consumer lifecycles.

PK06.title: Adhesive Impact on Sorting Efficiency
PK06.summary: Water-soluble and low-tack adhesives improve flake separation during recycling processing.
PK06.supports: Water-soluble and low-tack adhesives improve flake separation during recycling processing.

PK07.title: Rigid HDPE Density & Yield Optimization
PK07.summary: Optimizing wall thickness reduces resin consumption while passing drop-test requirements.
PK07.supports: Optimizing wall thickness reduces resin consumption while passing drop-test requirements.

PK08.title: Aluminum Barrier Foil Recyclability
PK08.summary: Thin aluminum layers require mechanical separation testing to ensure compatibility with standard sorting streams.
PK08.supports: Thin aluminum layers require mechanical separation testing to ensure compatibility with standard sorting streams.

PK09.title: Bio-based Polymer Performance Benchmark
PK09.summary: PLA and bio-PET offer compostable or renewable origins but require specific industrial composting infrastructure.
PK09.supports: PLA and bio-PET offer compostable or renewable origins but require specific industrial composting infrastructure.

PK10.title: Secondary Packaging Shrink-Film Reduction
PK10.summary: Replacing secondary shrink wrap with banded multi-packs cuts polymer usage by up to 50%.
PK10.supports: Replacing secondary shrink wrap with banded multi-packs cuts polymer usage by up to 50%.

PK11.title: Closure & Pump Mechanism Recyclability
PK11.summary: Springless mono-material dispensing pumps prevent sorting contamination in automated material recovery facilities.
PK11.supports: Springless mono-material dispensing pumps prevent sorting contamination in automated material recovery facilities.

PK12.title: Supply Chain Distance & Weight Correlation
PK12.summary: Mass reduction directly correlates with freight fuel savings across distribution networks.
PK12.supports: Mass reduction directly correlates with freight fuel savings across distribution networks.

PK20.title: Shampoo Recyclability and Component Specification
PK20.summary: Defines material sorting and stream compatibility for advanced shampoo container formats.
PK20.supports: Defines material sorting and stream compatibility for advanced shampoo container formats.

PK21.title: Advanced Shampoo Container and Dispenser Compatibility
PK21.summary: Evaluates specialized surfactant and dispenser compatibility for high-volume shampoo configurations.
PK21.supports: Evaluates specialized surfactant and dispenser compatibility for high-volume shampoo configurations.

PK30.title: Advanced Shampoo Sustainable Packaging Specification
PK30.summary: Evaluates specialized sustainable components and design criteria for advanced shampoo configurations.
PK30.supports: Evaluates specialized sustainable components and design criteria for advanced shampoo configurations.

PK31.title: Advanced Shampoo Packaging and Dispenser Evaluation
PK31.summary: Evaluates specialized dispenser design and packaging criteria for advanced shampoo configurations.
PK31.supports: Evaluates specialized dispenser design and packaging criteria for advanced shampoo configurations.

PK13.title: EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)
PK13.summary: Mandates recyclability performance grades and strict limits on empty space ratios for commercial packaging.
PK13.supports: Mandates recyclability performance grades and strict limits on empty space ratios for commercial packaging.

PK14.title: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Fee Structures
PK14.summary: Fees scale proportionally with material recyclability grade and recycled content percentages.
PK14.supports: Fees scale proportionally with material recyclability grade and recycled content percentages.

PK15.title: Single-Use Plastics Directive Compliance
PK15.summary: Prohibits specific problematic polymers and enforces reduction targets for high-impact formats.
PK15.supports: Prohibits specific problematic polymers and enforces reduction targets for high-impact formats.

PK16.title: Green Claims Substantiation Standards
PK16.summary: Requires transparent, verifiable lifecycle data before marketing packaging as eco-friendly or sustainable.
PK16.supports: Requires transparent, verifiable lifecycle data before marketing packaging as eco-friendly or sustainable.

PK17.title: Food-Contact Material Migration Limits
PK17.summary: Regulates chemical leachates and PCR purity thresholds for cosmetic and personal care contact layers.
PK17.supports: Regulates chemical leachates and PCR purity thresholds for cosmetic and personal care contact layers.

PK18.title: Recycling Infrastructure Sorting Mandates
PK18.summary: Establishes automated optical sorting recognition standards for municipal recovery facilities.
PK18.supports: Establishes automated optical sorting recognition standards for municipal recovery facilities.

PK19.title: Cross-Border Packaging Tax Frameworks
PK19.summary: Applies non-recyclable plastic packaging levies based on national weight quotas.
PK19.supports: Applies non-recyclable plastic packaging levies based on national weight quotas.
